newsitem.title: USA: Southern Baptists call for ban on human cloning.
newsitem.headline: Southern Baptists call for ban on human cloning.

text.p: Southern Baptists Thursday called for an international ban on cloning human beings but said they supported genetic engineering when aimed at curing diseases.

Delegates of the Southern Baptist Convention, which has 15.7 million members and is the nation's largest Protestant denomination, approved a resolution which urged Congress to legislate against human cloning.
"We call on Congress to pass a legal ban on cloning human beings in the United States and work toward international policy to make cloning human beings illegal around the world," the resolution said.
But it also said genetic technology should be used where it could help eradicate illnesses.
"We are not opposed to genetic technology, we are not even opposed to some forms of genetic engineering," said Rev. Richard Land, president of the Southern Baptists' Christian Life Commission.

"When we can go in and take out the gene that causes cystic fibrosis, for example, then God praise the ability of human beings to think God's thoughts after him," he said. "There is no absolute conflict between science and technology and the Christian faith."

President Bill Clinton earlier this month proposed a five-year ban on human cloning. Debates on the issue took on a sense of urgency after scientists in Scotland reported in February that they had successfully cloned a lamb from a single cell taken from an adult sheep.
The Southern Baptists Thursday ended a three-day annual meeting in Dallas, at which they launched a controversial boycott against Walt Disney Co. and its subsidiaries.
Southern Baptist leaders accused the entertainment giant of following "anti-family, pro-gay" policies and promoting homosexuality in its films and television shows.
